#!/bin/sh
set -eu
# Le interfacce Kathara sono gia attive; configurazione IPv4 ripetibile.
ip -4 address show dev eth0 | grep -Fq 'inet 10.16.1.11/24 ' || ip address add 10.16.1.11/24 dev eth0

ip route replace default via 10.16.1.1 dev eth0

# Associazioni ARP permanenti per i dispositivi direttamente collegati.
ip -4 neigh replace 10.16.1.1 lladdr 02:00:00:aa:01:01 nud permanent dev eth0
ip -4 neigh replace 10.16.1.12 lladdr 02:00:00:aa:01:03 nud permanent dev eth0
ip -4 neigh replace 10.16.1.13 lladdr 02:00:00:aa:01:04 nud permanent dev eth0
ip -4 neigh replace 10.16.1.14 lladdr 02:00:00:aa:01:05 nud permanent dev eth0

# Prevenzione timeout di startup: warmup ICMP limitato, non bloccante.
# Non modifica route, gateway o servizi.
probe_attempt=0
while [ "$probe_attempt" -lt 8 ]; do
  if ping -n -I eth0 -c 1 -W 1 10.16.1.1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  probe_attempt=$((probe_attempt + 1))
  [ "$probe_attempt" -lt 8 ] || break
  sleep 1
done

item.text: The lab already has static routes between its 15 LANs, so I can keep the network topology intact. I’m configuring a DNS server on pc1 and pointing the lab machines to it, with address and MX records derived from the existing startup files.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
zones=list(Path('pc1/etc/bind/lab').glob('db.*'))
records={}
for f in zones:
 for line in f.read_text().splitlines():
  m=re.fullmatch(r'(\\S+) IN (A|MX) (.+)',line)
  if m: records[(m[1],m[2])]=m[3]
assert sum(t=='A' and n"'!='"'ns' for n,t in records)==27
for domain in ['company.com','university.edu','dept.company.com','servizi.ministero.gov']:
 target=records[(domain+'.','MX')].split()[1]
 assert (target,'A') in records
for f in Path('.').glob('*.startup'):
 assert 'nameserver 10.16.1.11' in f.read_text(), f
print('Validated 27 address records, 4 MX targets, and DNS configuration on all 72 machines.')
PY
for f in *.startup; do sh -n \""'$f" || exit; done
printf '"'Startup scripts pass shell syntax checks.\\n'
command -v named-checkconf || true
command -v kathara || true"

item.text:
Configured DNS on pc1 for the requested hostnames and four mail domains. All 60 PCs and 12 routers now use it for name resolution; their existing addresses, routes, and connections remain unchanged.

The configuration contains 27 address records and four MX records. I checked that each MX target has an address and that all startup scripts pass shell syntax checks. I couldn’t run a live DNS or cross-network test because Kathara and BIND’s validation tools are unavailable in this environment.
